title: Operators
description: Understanding functions, parameters, return values, and scope.

lessons.title: What are Operators?
lessons.content: Operators are special symbols or keywords that perform operations on one or more operands (values or variables). They allow us to manipulate data and perform calculations or logical evaluations.

lessons.title: Arithmetic Operators
lessons.content:
let a = 10;
let b = 5;
console.log(a + b); // 15
console.log(a - b); // 5
console.log(a * b); // 50
console.log(a / b); // 2
console.log(a % b); // 0 (modulus operator)

lessons.title: Assignment Operators
lessons.content:
let x = 20;
x += 5; // equivalent to x = x + 5
x -= 10; // equivalent to x = x - 10
x *= 2; // equivalent to x = x * 2

lessons.title: Comparison Operators
lessons.content:
console.log(5 == '5');  // true (loose equality)
console.log(5 === '5'); // false (strict equality)
console.log(5 != 10);   // true
console.log(5 > 3);     // true
console.log(5 <= 5);    // true

lessons.title: Logical Operators
Ternary Operator
Typeof Operator
lessons.content:
console.log(typeof 42);       // 'number'
console.log(typeof 'hello');  // 'string'
console.log(typeof true);     // 'boolean'
// Useful to check the data type of variables or expressions.

lessons.title: Operator Precedence
lessons.content: Operator precedence determines the order in which operators are evaluated. For example, multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so it is performed first unless parentheses are used to override the order.

lessons.title: Short-circuit Evaluation
lessons.content: Logical operators like AND (&&) and OR (||) evaluate expressions from left to right and stop as soon as the result is determined. This is known as short-circuit evaluation and can be used to optimize code execution.

lessons.title: Bitwise Operators
lessons.content: Bitwise operators work on the binary representation of numbers, allowing manipulation at the bit level. They are less common but useful in performance-critical applications or when interacting with low-level data.
